name: Component Reflections Generate Every Fixed-Shadow Ample Family
statement: Fix a simplicial complex $\Sigma\subseteq2^F$ and a coordinate order $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. Starting from the down-set $D_\Sigma=\{x\in Q_F:\{f:x_f=1\}\in\Sigma\}$, reverse the coordinate down-shifts in that order: at each coordinate, independently choose a bit for every connected component outside the current reduction and apply the component-label expansion; if the reduction is empty, retain or reflect the constant coordinate. The outputs are exactly all ample families $H$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(H)=\Sigma$. For the prescribed order, every output uniquely determines all intermediate families and component choices. Consequently the graph of fixed-shadow ample realizations, with an edge for reflecting one component in one coordinate, is connected.
proof: Moving every unique lift in coordinate $e$ to layer zero preserves ampleness and the shadow; on the signed minimal-nonface presentation it sets the $e$-bit of every clause containing $e$ to one and leaves every other bit unchanged. These normalizations commute. Applying all coordinates makes every missing trace all-one, producing exactly $D_\Sigma$. Reversing the normalizations and applying the component-label theorem reconstructs any target realization. After stage $j$, the intermediate family is $D_{e_{j+1}}\cdots D_{e_n}(H)$, so its clauses determine both the family and all recovered component labels uniquely. Reversing any realization's path to $D_\Sigma$ proves connectivity.
